answer: Item-response modeling unmasks coordinated graders. The ledger fits a Rasch model where each submission is an item and each grader a person with an ability estimate. Honest graders show independent error patterns, but a sable swarm of wallets run by one operator leaves correlated residuals no solo account has. The shale of identical misgrades across unrelated posts betrays one hand behind many keys. An attacker must let each identity err divergently, paying real independent judgment per wallet, not scripting one fable of uniform verdicts. Cost is N calibrated graders, not a copied score.
